episodes.213584: Daytime heating combined with monsoon moisture in place resulted in the development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across the higher terrain midday slowly moving south and southeast into nearby lower elevations during the afternoon and early evening hours. One of these thunderstorms resulted in a 58 mph wind gust at the Santa Fe Municipal Airport. Thunderstorms tapered off shortly after sunset with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.213621: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over the Lower Susquehanna Valley during the mid to late afternoon hours on July 9, 2026. Some of these storms produced downpours that resulted in localized flash flooding of primarily urbanized areas.
episodes.213624: A typical summertime pulse environment brought an isolated severe thunderstorm into Burke County GA during the late afternoon, which caused a couple instances of tree and power line damage.
episodes.213681: Thunderstorms that developed over Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of July 8, 2026, produced heavy rain across the area. This resulted in flooding, particularly across portions of Wilson County where numerous roads were reported flooded.
episodes.213685: A cold front approached and moved across northern VT during the afternoon of July 9th. A few thunderstorms developed in southern Quebec province and then moved into northern VT. One thunderstorm intensified across northern VT and resulted in producing damaging microburst wind gusts in the Burle, Lyndonville area of northeast VT.
episodes.213686: During the early morning hour of July 9th, storms brought damaging wind gusts and heavy rainfall to far eastern Kansas.
episodes.213708: During the early morning hours of July 9th, storms brought damaging wind gusts to portions of primarily western Missouri.
episodes.213724: A lingering hot and humid airmass resulted in a few lines of thunderstorms as a front crossed the region. Moist atmospheric profiles inhibited more widespread or significant damaging wind gusts, though some storms did at least briefly become strong to severe.

episodes.213788: A second round of severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of July 7 across northern and northeast South Dakota. Peak wind gusts included 72 mph in Akaska (Walworth County), 71 mph at the South Dakota State University mesonet station 10 miles west-southwest of Aberdeen, 70 mph at the South Dakota State University mesonet station seven miles south of Claremont, and 68 mph at the Aberdeen Regional Airport Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) all in Brown County. Hail to the size of quarters was observed 5 miles west of the town of Webster (Day County) and in the town of Selby (Walworth County). ||Heavy rainfall was observed across northeast South Dakota, which resulted in flash flooding and river flooding. 5.18 inches was recorded by the CoCoRaHS observer in Claremont, the COOP observer in Webster observed 4.72 inches, and the automated COOP station at Sand Lake logged 4.39 inches. Many of the COOP and CoCoRaHS observers from in and around Aberdeen and points east in Day, Marshall and Grant counties recorded around 2.50 to 3.50 inches of rainfall. Around 2 inches of rain was recorded by the COOP and CoCoRaHS observers in and around the Watertown area as well. ||Flash flooding struck Aberdeen, stranding multiple vehicles in water near 24th Avenue Northwest (Fairgrounds Road). Streets underwater by as much as 1 foot were reported  primarily on the north side of town and eroding storm sewer infrastructure created a sinkhole at 1st Avenue Northeast and North Pennsylvania Avenue. The Marshall county Emergency Manager relayed that flooding around Newport Colony had resulted in roads under water and washouts. Runoff triggered river flooding along Moccasin Creek, Mud Creek, Willow Creek, the South Branch Tributary of Mud Creek, and the Big Sioux River.
episodes.213809: Isolated thunderstorm activity during the afternoon of July 9 resulted in some areas of minor tree damage in Shelby, Jefferson, and Marion counties. One storm produced a recorded gust of 56 mph, just below severe limits, at Bessemer Airport.
episodes.213948: Upper level high pressure was centered to the west of the combined Panhandles. This allowed the region to be situated under northwest flow in the upper levels of the atmosphere, which tends to promote storms to move into the region from the northwest. As temperatures climbed into the upper 90s to lower 100s, the hot airmass combined with plenty of instability and the ability for storms to bring down wind energy from higher in the storm, storms that occurred were able to bring damaging winds to the region.
episodes.213949: As thunderstorms developed across portions of New Mexico and Colorado, they moved southeast along the eastern edge of an upper level high pressure system. These storms brought damaging winds with them given plenty of dry air aloft that could be brought down to the surface in the more severe storms.
episodes.214040: Thunderstorms developed in a very unstable atmosphere. There was enough flow for storms to be moving, but some storms trained over one another, resulting in an isolated instance of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of two to four inches were observed.
episodes.214041: Thunderstorms developed in a very unstable atmosphere. There was enough flow for storms to be moving, but some storms trained over one another, resulting in an isolated instance of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of two to four inches were observed.
episodes.214211: A stationary front stalled across the Ohio Valley region, sparking showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.214368: A warm front tracking through the Mid-Atlantic produced heavy rain and subsequent flash flooding across portions of New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware.
episodes.214371: A warm front tracking through the Mid-Atlantic produced heavy rain and subsequent flash flooding across portions of New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware.

episodes.214550: Thunderstorms tracked eastward across the Colorado plains during the afternoon and evening of July 8th. A few of the storms produced strong outflow winds with the strongest gust reaching 76 mph.
episodes.214553: Scattered thunderstorms moved east across eastern Colorado during the afternoon and early evening of July 9th. Most storms were sub-severe, but two 60 mph wind gusts were recorded over far northeast Colorado.
episodes.214581: For the second time this summer, heavy rain from thunderstorms across the upper Big Sioux River Basin brought rises to the Big Sioux River itself. The river gauges at both Estelline and Bruce both briefly rose into Minor Flood Stage before quickly falling by mid month.
episodes.214689: A surface low pressure system stalled over Arkansas for a couple days and an attendant boundary consisted of a stationary boundary that eventually became a warm front and lifted northward. However over this period of time, damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding would be noted across much of the state.
episodes.214756: A broad area of high pressure shifted sufficiently to allow moisture to creep into Utah, and in combination with strong daytime heating, resulted in daily convection with instances of severe and damaging wind gusts, as well as some flooding.
episodes.214950: A couple of waterspouts occurred off the coast of the Florida panhandle with one in the evening and one in the morning.
episodes.215036: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds across northern Ohio.
episodes.215037: An isolated thunderstorm produced strong wind gusts over Lake Erie.
episodes.215277: A subtle shortwave moving across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska on July 8 produced enough lift and instability to initiate thunderstorm development. Thunderstorms produced large hail, strong winds and flooding.
episodes.215283: A subtle shortwave moving across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska on July 8 produced enough lift and instability to initiate thunderstorm development. Thunderstorms produced large hail, strong winds and flooding.
episodes.215284: A subtle shortwave moving over Wyoming combined with ample monsoon moisture lead to strong thunderstorms and heavy rain in Nebraska.
episodes.215356: A thunderstorm produced damaging winds in parts of Montgomery County on the afternoon of July 9.
episodes.215444: Widespread storms developed across northeast Kansas late evening on July 8. Out of these storms, a more organized cluster moved southeast across the area into the early morning hours of July 9, producing widespread wind gusts of 60-65 mph winds and occasional wind damage.
episodes.215512: Another shortwave crossed the area and brought more thunderstorms with strong wind gusts. Locations along Interstate 80 in far eastern Sweetwater County and along Interstate 90 in eastern Johnson County recorded wind gusts of 58 mph.
episodes.215764: A mesoscale convective system tracked from north of St. Louis to near Terre Haute during the late afternoon and early evening, triggering scattered severe thunderstorms.  A wet microburst downed a few trees on the north side of Effingham while a second storm knocked down a tree limb in Lawrenceville.  Pockets of heavy rain occurred with an observer in Casey in Clark County measuring 3.50.
episodes.216056: A retreating cold front led to scattered showers and storms during the afternoon and evening hours. Some storms over the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain produced wind damage and hail.
episodes.216067: A severe thunderstorm wind gust was recorded at the Juniper Interchange mesonet site on interstate 84.
episodes.216157: Afternoon sea breeze convection produced a strong marine wind gust over Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.216197: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms moved through Missouri on July 9 and into the morning of July 10. The first round of severe thunderstorms came through portions of west central and central Missouri during the morning of July 9. This cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph winds, resulting in damage to numerous trees. A second round produced severe thunderstorms over central into south central Missouri on the evening and night of July 9 into the morning of July 10. This resulted in a brief tornado in Rolla, in addition to a few instances of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches were observed from Maries through Dent counties.
episodes.216287: Numerous outflow boundaries sat across eastern Iowa on the 9th as a weak storm system  moved across the area. Scattered showers and storms developed across the area and interacted with these outflow boundaries causing funnel clouds to develop during the afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.216337: A shortwave trough tracked through southern Canada and pushed a cold front through the state, leading to scattered thunderstorms across central North Dakota through the afternoon and evening. There were numerous reports of severe hail across central North Dakota, as well as damaging wind gusts, with the most damage across Wells and Stutsman County. The largest hail reported was 2.5 inches in diameter near Silva in Pierce County and near Heimdal in Wells County. The strongest estimated wind gust was 80 mph north of Streeter in Stutsman County, where there was notable tree damage, a couple of grain bins blown away, and a pole barn that lost its roof.
episodes.216491: Another day with moisture streaming over a high pressure brough more thunderstorms the region. Storms developed off the higher terrain and pushed east, growing upscale into a large line of storms as the pushed towards the Colorado and Kansas border. While doing so, they produced strong winds.
episodes.216533: Active weather was observed on a daily basis in West Virginia from July 6th to the 9th amid hot temperatures and ample moisture. Showers and strong thunderstorms fired up quickly each afternoon, filled with heavy downpours and damaging wind gusts. Downed trees and power lines were the main impacts with severe weather during this stretch of time, along with street flooding and creeks rising out of their banks. The active weather pattern stretched further into the month due to an encroaching frontal boundary that stalled over the region. Daily showers and storms then continued over West Virginia heading into the middle of the month.
episodes.216607: During the afternoon and evening hours of July 8, 2026, thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across portions of eastern Nebraska and southwest Iowa. The thunderstorms initiated along a cold front during the afternoon as it was draped from northeast Nebraska into northwest Iowa. Thunderstorm development became more widespread along the front into the evening as the boundary slowly tracked southward. The environment was primed with over 2500 J/kg of MLCAPE and DCAPE values exceeding 1000 J/kg, supporting the potential for damaging wind gusts.||Throughout the event, several wind gusts ranging from 58 to 75 mph were measured or estimated across the region. Notable impacts included a tree collapsing onto a home in Papillion, NE and additional tree damage in Lancaster county. Additionally, several personal weather stations measured severe wind gusts across Platte, Dodge, Washington, Sarpy, and Lancaster counties in Nebraska, as well as Shelby County in Iowa.

episodes.216716: An upper level disturbance, moving through weak northwest flow aloft, interacted with an unstable airmass featuring MLCAPEs around 3000 J/kg across the Mid-South by the afternoon of July 9, 2026. As a result, a complex of thunderstorms developed over southeast Missouri and moved into northeast Arkansas and the Missouri Bootheel. The instability combined with 15 to 30 knots of shear supported a few severe storms with damaging winds.

episodes.216718: Instability values climbed to over 3000 J/kg during peak heating on July 9, 2026. Isolated thunderstorms developed with a lone storm over northeast Mississippi producing damaging winds.
episodes.216811: During the late evening hours on the 8th, a cluster of thunderstorms moving east to southeast over far northwest Kansas produced a measured 59 mph gust in Cheyenne County.
episodes.216839: Throughout much of the afternoon and evening on July 8th, severe storms moved slowly through northeast Iowa with several inches of rain in some locations. This resulted in isolated flash flooding along with rises into flood stage along portions of the Cedar and Upper Iowa River basins. Additionally, these storms produced severe wind gusts which resulted in scattered instances of tree damage.
episodes.216840: Repeated rounds of storms over portions of southeast Minnesota during the afternoon and evening hours on July 8th resulted in scattered instances of flash flooding during this timeframe. This included a closure of Interstate 90 due to flooding near Austin. The excessive rainfall also resulted in Dobbins Creek near Austin reaching into flood stage. Unrelated to flooding impacts, lightning from these storms struck a house in Winona which started a small fire.
episodes.216861: The beginning of an active monsoon period with a recorded wind gust of 70 mph in Sells that led to downed power lines and a power outage. Additionally, a severe thunderstorm moved off the Rincon and Catalina Mountains into the Tucson metro that caused a flag pole to bend and downed tree branches due to the strong winds.
episodes.216882: On July 9th, convection organized northwest of the border in Southern Ontario before crossing the Niagara River into Niagara County and the northern Niagara Frontier. |The SPC Severe Weather Outlook highlighted a Marginal Risk for the region, noting that shortwave energy moving out of Ontario would tap into localized instability ahead of a surface trough. NWS Buffalo's Area Forecast Discussions highlighted that these pre-existing Ontario storms were able to cross the lakes/river and maintain intensity into Western New York due to strong mid-level momentum and a well-instantiated low-level trough. As the convective cluster tracked into Niagara County (including the Pendleton report), the primary severe hazards were damaging straight-line wind gusts, frequent cloud-to-ground lightning, and localized torrential downpours.

episodes.217052: Severe thunderstorms brought large hail and damaging winds to parts of Eastern North Dakota during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.217141: A slow moving warm front and a trough resulted in scattered thunderstorm development on July 9.
episodes.217164: A line of training storms resulted in 1-2 inches of rainfall and scattered instances of flash flooding across Wetzel, Marion, and Monongalia counties on the 9th.
episodes.217189: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms in the vicinity of a stationary front produced wind damage.
episodes.217257: Storms occurred across a few different sectors of southern MT, with hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter occurring across far SE MT, and winds up to 64 mph across south-central MT.
episodes.217323: Severe weather across northern New Hampshire was focused across Coos counties on July 9, 2026. The storms were characterized by a broken line of fast-moving multicell thunderstorms driven by an approaching surface cold front. A mid-level shortwave trough and an accompanying surface cold front pushed east-southeastward from southern Quebec and Vermont into northern New New England during peak diurnal heating. Deep-layer shear (30���40 kt) was sufficient to foster cell organization into broken linear segments.  Strong convective outflow winds and large hail caused damage in Lancaster New Hampshire as a well developed shelf cloud pushed through the Connecticut River Valley.
episodes.217395: Damaging winds associated associated with an isolated strong to marginally severe storm impacted West Carrol Parish.
episodes.217437: A diffuse surface frontal boundary became the focus for scattered thunderstorm development early in the evening of July 9th. Most of these storms were sub-severe, however a few of the stronger storms did produce some marginally severe hail and an isolated thunderstorm wind damage report.

The Big Sioux River near Castlewood went into flood on the afternoon of July 9th as a result of multiple rounds of thunderstorms that delivered heavy rainfall across the southern Sisseton hills region on the evening of July 7th into the morning hours July 8th. The river crested at 9.26 feet, or 0.26 feet above flood stage during the early morning hours of July 10th and fell below flood later that morning. This level resulted in water over the culvert on 184th Street and the flooding of agricultural lands north of the town of Castlewood.
